title: (Scripture Reading Exercise.)
author: B. H. Roberts
note: Fifth Year (final) of the Seventy's Course in Theology. Focuses on divine immanence, the Holy Spirit, and nature of God.

footnotes.text: Doc. and Cov., Sec. lxxxviii:13. "The law and power by which all things are governed," is the late Elder Orson Pratt's foot note on the passage. See foot note "k" from verse 13.
There is a spirit in man; and the inspiration of the Almighty giveth them understanding; (Job xxxiii:8.)
Doc. and Cov., Sec. lxxxiv:45-47. See also St. John i:3-12.

From the nature of things one has to develop his subject gradually, "line upon line," and the writer suggests that the student, if he finds the statement not fully established as here made, that he await its fuller statement in later pages.
St. John x:30; xvii:22, et seq.
Seventy's Year Book III, Lesson XXXV.
I have so treated it in my Mormon Doctrine of Deity, pp. 166-169; also in the Seventy's Year Book No. III, Lesson XXXV.
Discourse by Pres. Brigham Young, June 13, 1852. Deseret News, Vol. 4, No. 6.
